justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements (R-01 to R-04) are fully addressed by dedicated elements: Video Consultation Service for consultations, Clinical Core & E-Prescription Service for prescriptions, AI Symptom Checker Service for triage, and Consent & Identity Management Service for purpose-based consent.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Performance is thoroughly supported by Mediasoup SFU Router, Adaptive Transcoder, Outbox Event Dispatcher with Cloud Pub/Sub, and caching via Local Credential Cache Component and Redis Room State Manager.
justifications.compatibility: R-08 is satisfied via Interoperability Mapper Component and EU/US Pharmacy Adapter Components supporting HL7 FHIR, SOAP, and REST to connect to External Pharmacy Gateways, alongside OIDC/OAuth2 federation with Identity Providers.
justifications.usability: Patients and Clinicians connect directly to API Gateway / BFF, but dedicated frontend interfaces or client applications (web/mobile portals) tailored to each distinct user group are omitted from the container model.
justifications.reliability: R-06 degraded mode is directly addressed by Bandwidth Throttling & Adaptation Module and Adaptive Transcoder. Reliability is bolstered by Buffer & Resiliency Manager, Local Credential Cache Component, and transactional outbox messaging.
justifications.security: Addresses GDPR/HIPAA with Consent Enforcement Validator, OPA Policy Sidecar, CMEK data encryption, Prescription Validation & Signer Component, Break-Glass logging, and Regional Model Gateway enforcing regional data residency.
justifications.maintainability: High maintainability achieved via well-bounded microservices, decoupled asynchronous messaging via Cloud Pub/Sub and Outbox Event Dispatcher, and reusable sidecars like Audit & Compliance Logger Sidecar and OPA Policy Sidecar.
justifications.portability: Services leverage containerized runtimes (Go, Node.js, Python, Java) across GCP regions (europe-west3, us-central1). However, tight dependencies on proprietary GCP services (Cloud SQL, Cloud Pub/Sub) without an abstraction layer slightly limit cross-cloud portability.

PERF-01.justification: The SFU Router (Mediasoup) and TURN/STUN cluster provide dedicated real-time media routing and scaling. However, the model lacks explicit auto-scaling policies and distributed SFU clustering details to definitively ensure sub-10s join times under sudden 5,000 concurrent session bursts.
sensitivity_points: SFU horizontal auto-scaling and signaling connection capacity under peak concurrency
tradeoffs: Lower signaling latency versus increased resource overhead of maintaining warm SFU nodes

PERF-02.justification: FastAPI handles high async throughput (~14 RPS for 50,000/hr) and delegating to Regional Model Gateways offloads intensive compute. The 3s response measure depends directly on external regional LLM inference latency and throttling limits, which are external to platform control.
sensitivity_points: Latency and concurrency quotas of upstream regional LLM endpoints on GCP
tradeoffs: Model accuracy and complex prompt chains versus inference response time

AVAIL-01.justification: The architecture contains dedicated real-time adaptation components including the Media Quality Monitor, Adaptive Transcoder, and Bandwidth Throttling & Adaptation Module to downscale video/audio below 300 kbit/s. Clinical record operations remain decoupled via transactional outbox patterns, preventing data loss.
sensitivity_points: Threshold tuning for dynamic WebRTC bitrate and resolution degradation
tradeoffs: Video fidelity degradation traded off for continuous consultation connectivity

AVAIL-02.justification: The target cloud lists only a single US region (us-central1). The architecture provides no secondary US region or automated failover mechanisms for US compute and Cloud SQL storage, making recovery within 1 hour without cross-border data transfer improbable.
sensitivity_points: Absence of a secondary disaster recovery region within US jurisdiction
tradeoffs: Strict data residency enforcement versus cross-region disaster recovery availability

MOD-01.justification: The architecture cleanly isolates format conversions within the Interoperability Mapper Component and encapsulates destination-specific integrations inside the modular EU/US Pharmacy Adapter Components, ensuring additions are strictly confined to a single adapter without impacting core clinical logic.
sensitivity_points: Decoupling of national prescription format mapping from core domain entities
tradeoffs: Adapter modularity overhead versus agility in supporting diverse country standards

MOD-02.justification: The AI Symptom Checker Service features an Inference Orchestrator and Regional Model Gateway supporting version updates, alongside a Traceability & Audit Emitter and Audit & Traceability Store that explicitly log inputs and model versions for full EU MDR traceability and rollback.
sensitivity_points: Immutable tracking of model version identifiers alongside patient inference payloads
tradeoffs: Storage overhead of comprehensive audit logging versus regulatory auditability

SEC-01.justification: Cross-region access is mediated by the Tenant & Region Context Resolver and Consent Enforcement Validator, which queries the Consent & Identity Management Service and evaluates policies via OPA Sidecars. Denials and accesses are logged via the Audit & Compliance Logger Sidecar.
sensitivity_points: Low-latency OPA policy evaluation enforcing regional data boundaries and active consent
tradeoffs: Strict zero-trust cross-region validation latency versus clinical record access speed

SEC-02.justification: Consent withdrawal is recorded in the Consent Ledger Component, which emits domain events via the Consent Revocation Broadcaster through Cloud Pub/Sub. The Local Credential Cache and OPA Sidecar ensure policy invalidation propagates near real-time, well within the 24-hour window.
sensitivity_points: Reliable broadcast and immediate eviction of cached consent permissions
tradeoffs: Asynchronous revocation eventual consistency versus immediate synchronous invalidation blocking
